title: DAL: A Practical Prior-Free Black-Box Framework for Piecewise Stationary Bandits
claim: Across many non-stationary environments and bandit variants, our method consistently attains the lowest cumulative regret versus all competing baselines.
layout: 4×5 grid of line plots, shared legend below, rows by change type
description: A 4-row by 5-column grid of line plots showing dynamic regret (y-axis) versus environment steps (x-axis, up to 5×10^4). Columns correspond to bandit variants: linear, generalized linear, structured/sparse contextual, kernel, and contextual bandits. The first three rows are piecewise-stationary settings with increasing change parameter ξ = 0.4, 0.6, 0.8. The bottom row is the drifting case. Each panel plots about a dozen colored lines with shaded confidence bands, including the proposed DAL variants (solid blue and dashed red) and baselines such as MASTER, ADA-OPKB, WeightUCB, Discounted, Sliding-Window and Budget-Restart. In nearly every panel the two DAL curves sit clearly lowest and the baselines fan out above them. Two rows of legend entries below the grid identify each method by color and line style.
caption: Dynamic regret vs. environment steps for synthetic experiments (lower$=$better). First three rows correspond to the geometric change-points and the final one to the drifting case. DAL attains the lowest dynamic regret across all different scenarios.
abstract: We introduce a practical, black-box framework termed Detection Augmented Learning (DAL) for the problem of piecewise stationary bandits without knowledge of the underlying non-stationarity. DAL accepts any stationary bandit algorithm with order-optimal regret as input and augments it with a change detector, enabling applicability to all common bandit variants. Extensive experimentation demonstrates that DAL consistently surpasses all state-of-the-art methods across diverse non-stationary scenarios, including synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets, underscoring its versatility and scalability. We provide theoretical insights into DAL's strong empirical performance, complemented by thorough empirical validation.
